newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ATHLETICS-BAILEY TRAILS IN SECOND IN MOSCOW MONSOON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY TRAILS IN SECOND IN MOSCOW MONSOON.

text.p: Olympic 100 metres champion Donovan Bailey trailed in second to Nigeria's Davidson Ezinwa at an IAAF Grand Prix meeting in Moscow which was all but washed away by monsoon-type rains on Sunday.

The Canadian sprint star, making his first appearance since beating U.S. 200 metres champion Michael Johnson in their $1.5 million 150-metre showdown in Toronto on June 1, clocked 10.28 seconds, eight hundredths behind the Nigerian.
Heavy rain swamped the track at times, thwarting results throughout the competition.
Nonetheless, Nigeria's Bisi Afolabi set the fastest women's 400 metres time of the season.

Team mate Falilat Ogunkoya completed a Nigerian one-two on the Lokomotiv track, clocking 50.79 seconds, just behind the 50.55 set by Afolabi, who has started her season looking to improve on her last place finish in the Olympic final last year.

Britain's former Olympic champion Sally Gunnell, back on the track after an injury in Atlanta, clocked 55.30 to finish second in the women's 400-metre hurdles to Tatyana Kereshchuk of Ukraine. Kereshchuk ran the distance in 54.96.
Double Olympic champion Svetlana Masterkova again proved she was Russia's top woman athlete, winning the 800 metres comfortably in one minute 59.26 seconds.
Kenyan athletes took the first four places in the men's 3,000 metres, with world record holder Daniel Komen winning in seven minutes 37.64 seconds.
Olympic champions Balazs Kiss of Hungary and Andrei Abduvaliyev of Uzbekistan disappointed in the hammer, taking fifth and seventh places respectively.
Atlanta winner Jean Galfione of France was first in the pole vault with a leap of 5.80 metres, while Barcelona champion Maxim Tarasov managed only fifth.
